title: 2-Year Floating Rate Note auction (second and final reopening of the October new issue) — the last leg of the $86B stamped spread, on a day the closing-time question is already settled
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched by plain curl and re-derived independently 2026-09-09 for this initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), text layer inflated stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 232 visual rows and 213 auction records — the same 213 the proposing sweep reached, reproduced from scratch rather than copied. Row reads verbatim `2-Year FRN R / Announcement Thursday, December 17, 2026 / Auction Wednesday, December 23, 2026 / Settlement Monday, December 28, 2026`; the trailing `R` marks a REOPENING and the quarterly cycle (new issue in the last week of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct, first reopening the following month, second the month after) places it as the SECOND reopening of the 2026-10-28 new issue. Size $28B: sb0590's alternating FRN column plus 12 consecutive reopenings accepted at exactly $28.00B since 2025-03-26 (fiscaldata auctions_query, floating_rate:Yes, 154 auctions 2014-01-29 to 2026-08-26, HTTP 200, re-pulled 2026-09-09). Stays estimate on two counts: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-17 announcement itself. The `TSY:` confirmed prefix in market-events-data.ts covers a treasury.gov auction schedule and is deliberately NOT taken for those two reasons.
notes: CANONICAL FILE written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, after reading in full the single proposal that existed for this id (proposals/treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23.from-treasury-2y-frn-2026-11-24.json) per EVENT-RESEARCH.md. THE HEADLINE, AND IT DEMOTES THIS EVENT'S OWN BILLING: the parent proposed this date as the SECOND DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION between a same-day congestion rule and a holiday rule. It is not one, because the holiday rule is already dead and the tape killed it years ago. December 23 is itself the natural experiment — four prior FRN auctions have fallen on that exact date with the holiday held constant, and the closing time tracks the same-day BILL count perfectly: 2014-12-23 one bill 11:30, 2015-12-23 zero bills 11:30, 2020-12-23 two CMBs 01:00 PM, 2025-12-23 two bills 01:00 PM. FOUR OF FOUR, where the holiday reading is 2 of 4 on its own best date. THE MECHANISM, NEW TO THIS CALENDAR AND STRICTLY BETTER THAN THE PARENT'S: it is not the auction COUNT, it is the capacity of the 11:30 a.m. competitive window. Across all 2,227 auction days and 4,639 auctions since 2014-01-06 (auctions_query, HTTP 200, 726,093 bytes, re-pulled this session), the 11:30 window has NEVER held more than two securities — the distribution of securities-per-day at 11:30 is exactly {0: 264 days, 1: 626, 2: 1337, 3+: ZERO}. The FRN's slot then follows deterministically: two other same-day securities in the 11:30 window and the FRN takes 01:00 PM on 16 of 16 days; fewer than two and it stays in the morning on 138 of 138. That is 154/154 with ZERO exceptions, against 148/154 for the parent's raw auction-count rule, and it absorbs every exception the parent had to name rather than explain — 2014-04-29, 2020-12-23, 2021-01-27 and 2022-07-14 are all two-bill days, 2020-05-27 is a five-auction day whose 10:00 a.m. CMBs left only one security in the 11:30 window, and 2019-12-06 (11:00 AM, visible in the parent's own cross-tab but absent from its 149/154 tally) is a one-auction day. Because coupons close at 1:00 p.m. (Bonds 260/261, Notes 838/1,039) and bills at 11:30 (3,102/3,339), the operative forward input is the SAME-DAY BILL COUNT. FOR THIS DATE the slate is 2-Year FRN R + 20-Year BOND R + 17-Week BILL: one bill, so the window has room and the FRN keeps 11:30 AM. Two further lines of evidence agree — an FRN sharing a day with any Bond has printed 11:30 five times out of five (2016-06-22, 2022-03-23, 2022-06-22, 2023-08-23, 2024-02-21), twice with a 20-Year specifically, and an FRN sharing with a 17-Week bill is 36 of 37 at 11:30. SECOND RESULT, and it closes two standing limits with a primary this calendar had never read: 31 CFR Part 356, fetched from the eCFR renderer 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 394,009 bytes). (a) The definitions section reads verbatim `Spread means the fixed amount over the life of a floating rate note that is added to the index rate ... the spread will be equal to the high discount margin at the time a new floating rate note is auctioned` — so treasury-2y-frn-2026-10-28's 51/51 and 103/103 spread-inheritance identity is a REGULATORY DEFINITION, not an empirical regularity, and it is upgraded here from a base rate to law (independently reproduced this session at 51/51 constant-spread CUSIPs and 51/51 new issues where HDM equals spread). (b) Appendix B section I paragraph C reads `accrued interest for a particular calendar day in an accrual period is calculated by using the index rate from the most recent auction of 13-week bills that took place before the accrual day ... However, the rate determined in a 13-week bill auction that takes place in the two-business-day period prior to a settlement date or interest payment date will not be used`, with the worked example naming a `two-business-day lockout period`. That is the published mechanism behind the settlement-precedence rule the 11-24 sibling fitted, and it closes that ledger's own limit that the rule was `inferred from 152/154, not read from 31 CFR 356`. A FIT CORRECTION FALLS OUT: the parent's rule as literally written scores 151/154 in this session's reproduction against the same 675-auction 13-week bill series, not 152/154 — the extra miss is 2019-12-18, where the most recent Monday bill settling before the FRN was itself auctioned FIVE DAYS AFTER the FRN, a physically impossible index. Adding the constraint that the index bill be auctioned no later than the FRN restores 152/154 with the parent's own two misses (2019-01-29, shutdown-shifted Tuesday bill slate; 2024-12-24, genuine and still unexplained). The 11-24 answer is unchanged. INDEX FOR THIS AUCTION: 2026-12-21, forced by the schedule rather than inferred — the Monday 12-21 13-week bill settles Thursday 12-24, four days before this FRN's 12-28 settlement and outside any two-business-day lockout, while the next bill (auctioned 12-28) settles 12-31, after. UNLIKE 2026-11-24 the index is set AFTER this event's own 12-17 announcement, i.e. the ordinary ordering, and the 2024-12-24 failure mode — a candidate bill settling exactly ONE business day before the FRN — is absent here. THIRD RESULT, and it is the demand-side variable this calendar has been pooling away: the concession is a LEG effect, not a calendar effect. Paired within CUSIP, the second reopening clears +1.31bp wider than the first reopening of the same security (n=50, t=3.14, positive in 32 of 50 cycles); unpaired, leg 1 runs +0.23bp (sd 2.80) against leg 2 at +1.54bp (sd 4.68). THE HONEST HALF: on 2021-06+ the paired effect collapses to +0.36bp (n=21, t=0.80) — significant over twelve years, ABSENT in the current regime, so it is recorded and not traded. December second reopenings are a MEAN NULL against other second reopenings (+2.78bp vs +1.15bp, Welch t=0.76) but carry roughly four times the variance (sd 7.14 vs 3.64, F=3.86; F=2.76 excluding the 2015-12-23 ZIRP outlier at +16.2bp). Consequence for the calendar: the 11-24 sibling's +/-4.0bp band was calibrated on a leg-1-dominated Thanksgiving pool and holds only 5 of 12 December second reopenings; the honest band for THIS cohort is +/-8.0bp (9/12 December leg 2, 20/21 leg 2 since 2021-06, 47/50 all leg 2). FOURTH: the day's macro block does not reach this security. 2026-12-23 carries PCE (high, confirmed), GDP Q3 third, durable goods and new home sales, all before an 11:30 auction — but the index is already fixed on 12-21, so a surprise can only move the margin, and a two-year floater has essentially no duration channel. The duration-sensitive security on the day is the 20-Year reopening, which bids at 1:00 p.m., AFTER this one. Sequencing: 08:30 macro, 11:30 FRN, 13:00 20-Year. DATA TRAP, reproduced from raw: a second reopening files under security_term `1-Year 10-Month`, never `2-Year`, so a `2-Year` filter drops it silently along with 103 of the 154 auctions in the series. Read-it-do-not-trade-it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed. Two dated adjacent events proposed in the same PR: treasury-20y-bond-2026-12-23 (same day, untracked, and the direct input to the closing-time call) and treasury-5y-tips-2026-12-22. Three forward tests registered in this event's own fragment, all scoring 2026-12-24. Ledger: docs/research/events/treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23.md.
